en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
1. The Mansion of the Female Slave (Dāsivimānavatthu) “Just like Sakka, the lord of the gods,
in the delightful Cittalatāvana grove;”
She wandered all around,
preceded by a host of women,
illuminating all directions.
Like stars and medicinal herbs.
By what means is your complexion such as this?
By what means do you attain success here?
And those riches arise that are dear to the mind.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
"What merit did you perform while you were a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty, and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?"
That deity, being delighted when questioned by Moggallāna,
answered the question that was asked.
The fruit of which deed is this?
"Among humans, having been born as a human,
I was a slave in another's household, dependent on others."
I was a female lay follower of the illustrious Gotama, the one with vision;
for her, I possessed diligence.
In the teaching of that Tathāgata,
let this body break apart as it may;
there is no stability in it here.
The path of the five training rules is auspicious and blissful;
it is thornless and free from entanglement.
Uprightness is proclaimed by the virtuous;
behold the fruit of renunciation,
as this woman has attained it.
"I am the messenger of the King,
of Sakka, the wielder of power;
sixty thousand musical instruments— "
They bring me awakening:
Ālamba, Gaggaro, Bhīma,
Sādhuvādī, and Saṃsaya.
Pokkharā and Suphassā,
Viṇāmokkhā and the women;
Nandā and Sunandā as well—
Soṇadinnā, Sucimhitā,
Alambusā, Missakesī, and Puṇḍarīkā the fierce one.
Eṇīphassā, Suphassā,
Subhaddā, and Muduvādinī—
these and others were your wives.
The awakeners of the nymphs—
those deities approach me at the proper time and address me.
Come, let us dance and sing;
come, let us delight ourselves.
This is not for those who have performed no merit.
This delightful and charming Nandana grove, the great forest of the Thirty-three gods, belongs only to those who have performed meritorious deeds.
Happiness does not exist for those who have not performed merit,
neither in this world nor in the next;
but happiness belongs to those who have performed merit.
Both here and in the world beyond,
those who desire fellowship with them should perform much wholesome merit.
"For those who have performed merit rejoice in heaven, endowed with wealth.
Thus ends the first *Dāsī-vimāna*.
